req.title: Redirect-to supports custom status codes
req.statement: The system shall honour the 'status_code' query parameter on /redirect-to for values 301, 302, 303, 307, and 308.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to() handler reads 'status_code' from query args, validates it is in [300,400), and sets response.status_code accordingly. To kill mutations we must: (1) assert exact status codes for each valid value (301,302,303,307,308); (2) test the boundary at 300 (inclusive lower bound) and 399 (inclusive upper bound); (3) test 299 and 400 which must NOT be honoured (boundary ±1); (4) test missing status_code defaults to 302; (5) test the Location header is set to the exact url supplied. Each test uses follow_redirects=False so we see the redirect response directly.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_status_301
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_status_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_status_301()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_boundary_below_lower_299
expected: Response status code is exactly 302 (default), NOT 299, because 299 < 300 fails the >= 300 guard
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_boundary_below_lower_299():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=299', follow_redirects=False)
    # 299 is below the 300 threshold so the guard rejects it; default 302 must be used
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 299

test_redirect_to_boundary_below_lower_299()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_location_header_exact_url
expected: Location header equals exactly the url query parameter value
tests.executable:

def test_redirect_to_location_header_exact_url():
    target = 'https://www.google.com/search?q=test'
    r = client.get(
        '/redirect-to?url=https://www.google.com/search?q=test&status_code=307',
        follow_redirects=False
    )
    assert r.status_code == 307
    assert r.headers['Location'] == target

test_redirect_to_location_header_exact_url()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact
actions: Iterate over [301,302,303,307,308] and GET /redirect-to with each status_code
expected: Each response status code matches the requested code exactly
Location header is correct for each
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact():
    for code in [301, 302, 303, 307, 308]:
        r = client.get(
            '/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code={}'.format(code),
            follow_redirects=False
        )
        assert r.status_code == code, 'Expected {} got {}'.format(code, r.status_code)
        assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300
actions: GET with status_code=301 and separately with status_code=300 to confirm both are honoured
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300():
    r301 = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://a.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r301.status_code == 301
    assert r301.status_code != 302
    r300 = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://a.com&status_code=300', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r300.status_code == 300
    assert r300.status_code != 302

test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300()
